issues.description: The problem statement and UML define an interface named 'Milkable', and the template Main uses 'Milkable', but the solution repository introduces an interface named 'Dairy' (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Dairy.java) while the Milkable.java in the solution is empty. This name/type mismatch for the milkable interface is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students about which interface to implement and may break references in the template (Main) and tests that expect 'Milkable'.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent interface name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's 'Dairy' interface to 'Milkable' (or make Milkable a proper interface with the same method signature) and update all classes to implement 'Milkable'. Ensure the solution's Milkable.java contains the expected method signature 'String messageOnMilk();' so it matches the problem statement and the template Main references.

issues.description: The exercise describes a Milkable interface (methods like messageOnMilk()) and the template/Main references Milkable, but the solution implementation introduces an interface named Dairy (Dairy.java) which is implemented by Goat and Seal. This renaming (Milkable vs Dairy) refers to the same conceptual entity (animals that can be milked) with different identifiers across artifacts and will confuse students mapping the problem requirements to the solution and template code.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single interface name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's Dairy interface and its implementations to Milkable (rename Dairy.java -> Milkable.java, change interface declaration to 'public interface Milkable' and update Goat and Seal to 'implements Milkable'), or alternatively update the problem/template to consistently use Dairy. Prefer aligning the solution to the problem's 'Milkable' name so students can directly map requirements to code.
